los.text: Identify the structures that form during the development of the embryo and its supporting structures from fertilisation to 18 days, and recall the timings of the formation of these structures
los.html:
Day (after fertilisation)Event
0–1Fertilisation in the ampulla of the uterine tube → zygote
1–3Cleavage (2 → 4 → 8 cells) → morula (~16 cells) reaches the uterus
4–5Blastocyst: inner cell mass (→ embryo), trophoblast (→ placenta), fluid cavity; hatches from the zona pellucida
6–7Implantation begins (usually posterior uterine wall); trophoblast splits into cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast (invades, makes hCG)
8–14 ("week of twos")
  • Bilaminar disc (epiblast + hypoblast)
  • Two cavities (amniotic and yolk sac)
  • Two trophoblast layers
  • Extraembryonic mesoderm and chorionic cavity
  • Implantation complete ~day 10–12
15Primitive streak and node appear: start of gastrulation
15–16Epiblast cells migrate → trilaminar disc: ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm
16–18Notochord forms; it induces the neural plate (~day 18)
Germ layerGives rise to
EctodermEpidermis, nervous system, neural crest
MesodermMuscle, bone, connective tissue, heart and vessels, kidneys, gonads
EndodermLining of gut and its glands (liver, pancreas), respiratory epithelium, bladder
  • Supporting structures: amnion, yolk sac (first blood cells, primordial germ cells), chorion → placenta, connecting stalk → umbilical cord.

los.text: Recall the timings of the embryonic and foetal periods, the relation of embryological timings to clinical gestation timings, and recognise the principles of growth and development
los.html:
• Two clocks: embryological age counts from fertilisation
    • clinical gestational age counts from the first day of the last menstrual period, about 2 weeks more.
    • Term = 40 weeks gestation = 38 weeks after fertilisation.
PeriodWeeks after fertilisationWhat happens
Pre-embryonic1–2Fertilisation to bilaminar disc; teratogens are "all or none"
Embryonic3–8Organogenesis: most sensitive to teratogens; major malformations
Fetal9 to birthGrowth and maturation; insults cause growth or functional problems (brain stays sensitive)
Principles of development
  • Proliferation
  • Differentiation
  • Migration
  • Induction (one tissue signalling another, e.g. notochord → neural plate)
  • Apoptosis (e.g. separating the fingers)
  • Morphogenesis and folding (week 4: head-to-tail and side-to-side folding make the embryo a cylinder and pinch off the gut tube).
GrowthHead first (cephalocaudal): the head is about half the body length at 9 weeks.
